quick_skim.title: EDCT-Bench: Uncovering Faithfulness Gaps in VLMs via Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing
quick_skim.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can produce Natural Language Explanations (NLEs) that sound plausible yet remain inconsistent with the visual evidence they cite. We present Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing (EDCT), an intervention-based protocol that extracts visual concepts cited in a model's explanation, applies verified minimal edits to them, and tests whether the resulting answer and explanation remain consistent with the edited image. Using this protocol, we create EDCT-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark spanning three complementary domains: knowledge-intensive visual question answering (OK-VQA), safety-critical driving (DriveLM), and 3D spatial reasoning (3DSRBench). Across the evaluated VLMs, EDCT reveals substantial faithfulness gaps, with models frequently producing responses inconsistent with verified visual changes. Finally, our fine-tuning study suggests that EDCT-generated counterfactuals provide high-impact training signals.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Vision-language models can produce plausible explanations inconsistent with cited visual evidence. EDCT extracts visual concepts from explanations and applies verified minimal edits to test answer-explanation consistency, revealing substantial faithfulness gaps across knowledge VQA, driving and 3D spatial reasoning.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 视觉语言模型能生成听起来合理却与其所引用视觉证据不一致的自然语言解释，忠实性存疑。本文提出解释驱动的反事实测试协议EDCT，提取解释中引用的视觉概念，施加经验证的最小编辑，检验答案与解释是否仍与编辑后的图像一致。基于该协议构建的EDCT-Bench涵盖知识密集VQA、安全驾驶与三维空间推理三个领域，揭示被评模型存在显著忠实性缺口。研究为大模型解释忠实性评估提供了可干预的基准方法。
